I was a little worried that this antenna would be a waste of money, but I was wrong. After years of pixelation and moving my old rabbit ears around to try to get stations, I wanted to try something better. I have this going in to a digital converter box as I still have a tube TV. After messing around with the placement, I get more channels than before and I no longer have to worry about if where I sit in the room will affect my reception. Very good antenna!

power, and with a new converter box scan I was able to somewhat pick up WTMV and its 2 sub-channels, 29-1, 29-2, and 29-3. It was VERY scrambled, and then I tried messing around with the placement of the antenna, and subsequent converter box scans couldn't pick that station up anymore.

It has been years since I bought an antenna, and so, even with digital TV, I was a little skeptical. Setting it up where I wanted it to go served no issue whatsoever. I plugged in the antenna, positioned it with the help of the converter box, and found the ideal position. The picture is comparable to that of satellite, and I am really impressed. Not only can I watch the channels I want to watch, but I can also record any program with the best of quality.

Here in Ashford CT the rumor was we couldn't get any free to air stations. This antenna picks up 12-15 stations although I need to sit it in the window pointing West. Probably three of those channels come in maybe 60% of the time. Most of the channels are 30+ miles away with hills in the way and it still gets them.

This antenna did very poorly and was able only to get reception on 2 channels which formerly got 15 on old antenna .I would not recommend this product to anyone. I went back to old unit sold at Best Buy . It was a total waste of money.

I can put up with it.Be sure you buy the RIGHT Micron XG--apparently there is a UHF version and I think there is another version yet that comes without the amplifier. Even ClearStream's own website is confusing as to which version is which.And shop around--I paid about $40 too much. But it is still better than eating a $80 cable bill month after month.

We don't care that we don't have popular cable TV channels, e.g. HBO, Food Network, CNN, ESPN etc., because we still can have other great alternations, especially the internet has so much fun to enjoy. The only thing we need to do is just to connect the TV and computer.This product outlook is gorgeour and simple. It does not look not good when we put it besides the small windown platform.

I live in NYC and Time Warner has the monopoly in Manhattan. Local channels come in great with the exception of  channel 11. When using the amp u can get channel 11 and a few others as well. Also,my antenna box was opened and repacked  like it was a return. Not happy about that.
Sometimes the cables not working too great so I switch to this Antenna and get all the channels I need, never miss a show

These items arrived as promised, just ahead of a big weekend of chasing hot air balloons. The caps are spares, so I didn't need to use them, but I did snap on onto my lens and it appears to fit just fine and is made of heavy plastic...doesn't feel flimsy at all.The cap-keepers are wonderful! I really like the elastic to fit around the lens instead of hooking on to the strap anchor on the camera. It's much less in the way.

I recently purchased a Nikon D5200 single lens reflex camera and am quite happy with it, except for one thing. The lens caps that came on the lenses have the brand name NIKON deeply embossed on the middle of the outward facing portion of the lens cap. Very good looking, but unfortunately because of that embossing it is impossible to have the adhesive that holds the lens cap to the elastic that goes around the lens adhere to the lens cap.
I love this product. The band fits great around the lens. No more worrying where to put the lens cap!
Many similar elastic band retainers have bee criticized for falling off various lens caps and that may be the result of insufficient pressure when installing them.

The caps arrived a timely manner and were appropriately packaged for shipment. They fit the lens as advertised and the elastic band does an excellent job of holding onto the lens barrel. Completely satisfied with the quality and price.

I like tying the string to the lens cap through a small hole in the cap, rather than glueing a string holder to the front of the cap. To accomplish this one must connect the string to the cap, cut off the string holder from the stretchy part that goes around the lens, and then tie the two parts together. No big deal.

How often have you lost a lens cap? I have many times so I bought several of these and they are great and easy to use, especially with the nifty keeper. Just slip the elastic band on the lens itself and stick the sticky end on the lens cover and off you go!

These caps for my lens are awesome! I love that attaching the part to the cap is easy and it stays. I LOVE the elastic part which goes on and then keeps my cap right where I need it while using my camera. I then can find my cap and am never worried that I can't find my cap. It's a must have!

They have an elastic band that slips over the lens that is then attached to a nice little leash stuck to the cap. Those pesky lenses and their desire for freedom is now thwarted. And even if I happen to come across an extra crafty lens that some how gets loose, I have a few more in the package to take its place. They fit like the originals and I can't complain. Take that Lake Superior! You don't get any more of my caps!

I just received the lens caps earlier this week and put them to good use immediately. These lens caps fit my lenses very well, as they will on any 58 mm lens. While I am not going to use the elastic band, I believe I will try to use the cords that come without the elastic. This seems a better fit for my needs.I will definitely recommend this product to a friend . . . but not an enemy.

i read all the reviews before i bought this and didnt see many bad ones. but i had to hear for myself. all i can say is holy crap. this thing is so small and sounds so huge. i have it in a 07 saturn vue running it with a pyramid 1000watt artic amp. if you need space and huuuuge sound buy this. buy it now!!!!!!!! !

I ordered this not really expecting this much sound out of such a small box. I had an old Hifonics 50 x 50 amp that connected in bridge mode. This thing is awesome! Much more bass than I need. You will not hear it unless you are sitting in the truck and then it rocks. Vibrates the rear view mirror and the seats.

It sounds great, I have it running through an ancient RF punch amp and it hits HARD. Granted its an older RF amp and they are SERIOUSLY underrated. Its a sealed enclosure, so it"s a quick,  solid hard hitting bass, rather than a really deep ultra low tone bass. It does need to break in and i feel that it will only get better after break in.

Here's the review.While writing this I see the product title as Enclosure 800 Watts. Not sure if that is a mistake or what, but it is rated for 200 Watts. I am currently giving it 200 Watts (from a bridged RF 4 channel amp) and let me tell you, it will need no more. I've had sound systems that were insane in my younger days, so I know what to expect from a shallow mount 10" sub. I was surprised.

I was looking for a sub for my 2000 mustang ragtop to give me some bass when the top was down. Almost spent 600.00  plus at an electronics store, they said I would need a special setup to get bass. I read the reviews on this sub with the boss R1100M. Bought it, installed it, exceeded my expectations. Great sounding bass on the highway with the top down. The adjustable bass control that comes with the amp works great to adjust the sub to different music.

For "Maximum Bass" I can fold the rear seats forward and then really have to lower the gain on the remote gain control for the Boss amp or I get way more bass than I need. Had to change the low bypass filter setting from 100db to 80db on the head unit to get a less muddled sounding low end and the 6 X 9's do such a good job with this setting that it sounds perfect. I have only had this running for two days now and it is really impressive.
The two descriptions of the dimensions are different so I need to know the exact specifications of the length, width, and height. Somebody help!
If you are look for a compact sub/box, this is the unit you need. I am not a person that likes a high amount of bass. This unit has enough bass anybody needs.

Maybe it's just me. Probably this minor thing it's going to be address in the near future (hey, I said 'outstanding', not 'perfect'!

First off, 4 TVs can't watch independently, only 3 can. There are only 3 tuners on the Hopper. The Hopper "supports" 3 Joeys, but if you add a third Joey then one of the Joeys has to watch the same as one of the other TVs, or something recorded. This is VERY misleading advertising on Dish's part.We got the Hopper and 2 Joeys for a 3-TV two-story household.

You can still personalize favorite channels and the interface for doing that is great since it is clear to see what the channel is that you are selecting. I bought this for my nieces for Christmas. It's very cute and sturdy. Since I haven't given it to them yet, I can't tell you what they think of it, but after spending 3 1/2 hours putting it together last night, I can give you a few hints on assembly.First, it's definitely harder than Ikea. Ikea optimizes the assembly so that everything can be put together with one or two types of hardware. This is not the case here. If there is a board, it probably has it's own hardware. There are seven types of bolts and four types of screws. They organize the hardware nicely in a divided packet, but be very careful not to mix them up. Open only the ones you need from the pack by the perforated cardboard on the back. Don't mix up the matching bolts and nuts. They come attached to each other. I mixed them up at some point and they didn't attach easily, even though they were the same type of hardware.I was able to manage with the mini wrench and Allen wrenches supplied, but you do need a Philips screwdriver. It does need to be a real one, not one with

wrenches supplied, but you do need a Philips screwdriver. It does need to be a real one, not one with interchanges bits since the post holding up the curtain require you to insert the screw inside the post an inch or two and the hole wasn't wide enough to accommodate my interchangeable screwdriver.There are 35 pieces in the set and 22 steps. The steps, while do not have any text, are pretty clear. Be patient, make sure you've attached everything since there are usually many things to attach in each step. Step 1 is probably the hardest, so don't get discouraged. It essentially puts together the frame. Step 3 is a little visually confusing, but all it really means is that 26 gets attached with screw F and 7 gets attached with screw G. I did notice one slight error. For piece 7, the latch should be on top. It doesn't appear in diagram in Step 3 (which is shouldn't since this is a bottom view), but when you see the top view of the piece, in Step 4 it doesn't appear either (which is should). It doesn't show up until Step 6 so be careful which direction you assemble

doesn't appear either (which is should). It doesn't show up until Step 6 so be careful which direction you assemble it.I noticed small alignment issues. The back splash was a little tight and I had one back panel (piece 21) whose grooves on the bottom didn't align with the grooves on the side. It wasn't a huge misalignment, but enough that I had to loosen hardware and push and pull a little to work.So, in summary? I sleep with a sound machine next to my bed (my baby's shuts off after 20 min), and I can clearly hear him over that.I also like that the fact that if the baby unit fails or the power goes out, the parent unit immediately makes a horrendous beep.CONS:I don't like that there is no battery backup for the baby unit.Finally, I think that the ease of use could be better (hence 4 stars).

My baby is almost 3 years old. I've had several monitors over the years and I can tell you, for this price range this is as good as it gets. It has a great mic, you can definitely hear everything going on in the babys room: a clock ticking, the sound that the curtain makes, etc. Even if the baby breathes deeply and you have the parents unit on loud you can hear it perfectly. I like that about it.There is no static on mine at all.
This is a great monitor.I feel like I can hear everything going on in Baby's room, NO interference, no pesky channels to mess with.The design is beautiful.

I think this is the best choice out there for a monitor. It is lightweight and simple to use. Since it is digital, I have had no problem with interference. The sound quality is great, I can clearly hear the baby noises, even with background noises (white noise maker, music from the swing). The unique aspect of the monitor is the visual sound indicator. Bars of light come on when a new sound comes in-- the more bars, the louder the sound.

I registered for this product based on the high rating and chose to ignore some people who had complained about the volume :-(. Big mistake. One cannot hear the baby's small noises if there is TV, you are talking to someone, the bathroom fan is on etc. It is really painful. You can hear it if he is crying though - but I don't want him to have to cry to get our attention (that's the whole point of using a monitor, isn't it?

I purchased this monitor almost two years ago. I have packed it and moved it, dropped it on the floor, kicked it and it is still working. I can hear everything clearly...if I turn it up to the highest level I can hear my daughter breathing. Of course then if its at the highest level when she starts crying its REALLY loud. I really like it, though, and I especially like how it has lasted through my klutziness.

Overall, we do like this monitor. Our house is 3 stories and the bedrooms are on the top floor. We can go down to the basement level with the parent unit and still be within range. We can still hear everything with no problem. There is background noise, a slight hum, all the time, but we don't find it to be an issue.

This monitor is clear, but like other reviewers said it is far too quiet---you can only hear sounds on the parent unit if there's no background noise where you are. So this unit would probably be fine if you only want to use it at night, but we want to be able to use it during the day as well, so it's essentially useless to us. One other slight negative:  The parent unit only has a belt clip.

But this monitor is awesome! For me, it goes about 4 houses over (probably abour 450') and is perfectly clear. i sometimes have to check to make sure it's still on- it is just that quiet. yes, the light on the baby monitor does blink when you have the parent monitor off, but i just put my baby monitor on the opposite side of his room (about 12' away) and i can still hear him perfectly clearly on the second volume level.buy this monitor!!

The 85 psi max is fine for road: smooth (buttery, actually)and can be lowered to 50-55 for smooth gravel hardpack.
